page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.8-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. The server is configured with 16 dedicated Ampere AmpereOne-M physical cores running at one thread per core, providing 16 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading resource contention. The system provision includes 64 GB of memory, yielding an allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

This instance does not include integrated local storage and relies entirely on external block volumes for persistent data. Hardware accelerators such as discrete GPUs are absent, concentrating all compute resources on CPU execution and memory handling. Network connectivity features one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Because each vCPU corresponds to an independent physical core, the configuration avoids thread contention. The balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio makes the platform well aligned with distributed web services, container worker nodes, microservice architectures, continuous integration pipelines, and enterprise application servers.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.8-64 is a balanced general-purpose cloud instance powered by the 64-bit ARM Ampere AmpereOne-M processor family. It features 16 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, delivering 16 vCPUs without the variable resource competition typical of simultaneous multithreading. System memory totals 64 GB, providing a standard 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no local storage devices or discrete hardware accelerators, meaning all persistent storage must be attached via remote block storage volumes. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provided with the deployment. With its predictable single-thread-per-core design and balanced compute-to-memory configuration, the instance is engineered for horizontal application scaling, web application backends, container orchestration clusters, continuous integration agents, and microservices architectures.
